problem:
The substitution $z={y}^{3}$ can be used to transform the equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{{y}^{2}}-{x}^{2}y
$$

into an equation of the form ${z}^{′}(x)+P(x)z(x)=Q(x).$ What is the function $P(x)?$
worked_solution:
First, we make the substitution

$$
z={y}^{3}\,⟹\,y={z}^{1/3}.
$$

Differentiating $z(x)$ using the chain rule, we get 

$$
\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x}=3{y}^{2}\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,⟹\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{3{z}^{2/3}}\,\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x}.
$$

 

Consequently, the original differential equation can be written in terms of $z$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(\frac{1}{3{z}^{2/3}}\,\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x}) & =\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{{z}^{2/3}}-{x}^{2}{z}^{1/3} \\ \frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x} & =3\operatorname{sin}⁡x-3{x}^{2}z\end{aligned}
$$

Now we write the above equation in standard form

$$
\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x}+P(x)z=Q(x).
$$

Doing so, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x} & =3\operatorname{sin}⁡x-3{x}^{2}z \\ \frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x}+3{x}^{2}z & =3\operatorname{sin}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $P(x)=3{x}^{2}.$
